answer: Random witness lottery assigns each new identity a challenge seeded by a beacon committed before reveal, so attackers cannot precompute valid solutions. Enforcement requires a solution hashed through a prism below a threshold and a signature from a randomly selected witness chosen by the same seed. The wharf rejects duplicate attempts before admission, so each extra identity costs expected puzzle compute plus a forfeited fixed 100-unit deposit on a failed witness check. Only passing identities get a bridge credential, making bulk registration pay repeated unpredictable witness solicitation.
